points.text: Theory section confusing; Theorem 1 generic Lagrangian not tied to the specific losses
lambda has weak influence, questioning need for both loss terms; needs more datasets/models
Early decoding tokens never eligible for reflection due to entropy buffer warm-up
Experiments restricted to math datasets
Unclear why correction vector applied to all past tokens in CE loss
High-entropy triggers dominated by function words; content-aware trigger ablation missing
Self-consistency baselines limited; no prompt seeds, temperature sweeps, ToT under equal budget
Unclear whether compared results use comparable inference budgets
No thorough inference-cost analysis across temperature, length, correction frequency
Method expensive: up to 50% inference-time increase
No side-by-side comparison with other reasoning-improvement methods; SLOT on one model only
Only math competition benchmarks; no coding, logic or tabular reasoning
Combination with RL-based post-training methods not shown
No empirical comparison to decoding methods (DoLA, SLED) or critical-token methods
Multiple new hyperparameters contradict plug-and-play claim
Avoids head-to-head comparison with self-refinement/test-time baselines under matched compute
Evaluation almost only math tasks with math-tuned models
One model degrades with SRGen, contradicting consistent-gains narrative
Entropy trigger blind to confident errors; failure mode not analysed
Orthogonality/compatibility claims overstated; only combined with SLOT
Theorem 1 is textbook Lagrangian equivalence, little novelty
Theorem gives no guidance on choosing lambda or its generalisation
Self-referential delta optimisation without ground truth may reinforce model biases
Compatibility shown only with SLOT; not with training-free methods like contrastive decoding
Main table lacks comparison to other self-reflective methods
Benchmarks limited to mathematical problems
Table 2 missing percentage marks
Latency reported only as ratios, not absolute time
Notation t and k inconsistent; Avg@k defined using Pass@k before introduced
Section 5.4 does not discuss Avg@k
No baseline methods run, only base model; Table 1 ratings qualitative assertions
Missing lower-temperature/sharpened sampling and greedy decoding controls
Missing entropy/confidence-aware decoding baselines (DeepConf, forking)
Missing entropy-minimization test-time baselines (TENT-style)
Missing budget-matched alternatives such as more majority-vote samples
Missing random-trigger or fixed-interval ablation to test entropy trigger
Small 30-problem benchmarks; no seeds, CIs or significance; noisy Cons@5
Reported values inconsistent with 30 problems; metric computation unclear
Gains may come from reduced truncation/loops; no output-length analysis
Base numbers unusually low; non-standard setup; Qwen3 thinking mode unspecified
Mechanism likely logit sharpening; no evidence corrections fix errors at entropy spikes
CE-only ablation gains conflict with entropy-minimization being key
Theorem 1 textbook scalarization; no lambda guidance or convergence; overstated as guarantee
Applying delta to all earlier hidden states unjustified and not compared
Latency measured only on one model with short traces; 50% bound unshown for long traces
Cost model ignores prefix loss, caching unstated, memory overhead unreported
Ablations on 100 problems, one model; hyperparameters unchecked on reasoning models
SLOT combination only on one capped model
Only exact-answer math benchmarks despite broad reasoning claims
Text claims inconsistent with Table 2 results
Diversity loss from entropy reduction barely discussed
Code withheld until after review; evaluation details only in appendices
